screenshots.name: 01-login
screenshots.evidences: Section 3.15.2 — four roles are four separate sign-ins, not a role selector on one account.

screenshots.name: 02-buyer-escrows
screenshots.evidences: FR-02 — the buyer workspace lists only that buyer's escrows.

screenshots.name: 03-buyer-new-escrow
screenshots.evidences: Section 3.12.4 and FR-01 — the escrow creation form, whose submission is scored by the FastAPI model before any funds move.

screenshots.name: 04-buyer-escrow-detail
screenshots.evidences: Section 3.14 and Section 4.3.5 — one escrow in full: the risk score that admitted it, the features that drove that score, and the state the contract currently holds it in.

screenshots.name: 05-rbac-refusal
screenshots.evidences: Section 3.15.2 — the decisive shot. A buyer requesting /admin is refused server-side and redirected to /forbidden. The browser cannot assert a role it does not hold, because the session cookie is HttpOnly and signed with a server-held key.

screenshots.name: 06-seller-escrows
screenshots.evidences: Section 3.15.2 — the same route renders a different workspace for a different role; permissions are not stacked in one view.

screenshots.name: 07-arbitrator-disputes
screenshots.evidences: FR-05 and Section 3.11.1 — dispute resolution is reachable only by the arbitrator, matching resolveDispute's on-chain check against the escrow's recorded arbitrator.

screenshots.name: 09-admin-model
screenshots.evidences: Section 3.14 — the deployed model version and the risk threshold the contract enforces.

screenshots.name: 10-admin-settings
screenshots.evidences: Section 3.11.3 — the risk threshold is configuration, and the interface says so.

screenshots.name: 11-admin-audit
screenshots.evidences: Section 3.15.2 — the audit trail, which records the layer and the actor for every recorded event.
